messages:
Maria Chen: Ran an apples-vs-replay comparison on the 4-tenant CI cluster this morning. Continuous batching enabled (max_delay_ms=5, batch_cap=128). Observed a p95 latency regression for tenant-B vs the synthetic baseline. Putting raw numbers below. :thinking:
perf-bot: profile summary attached — kernel fallback events spike at sequence lengths >384, KV cache miss rate is very skewed across tenants (B is cold). Quick highlights:
  - tenant A p95: 42ms (baseline 38ms)
  - tenant B p95: 210ms (baseline 95ms)
  - overall throughput: near target but tail regressed
  - kv_cache hit_rate: A 82%, B 38%, C 70%, D 66%
Jake Patel: ouch. what's the workload shape for tenant B? longer sequences or more unique prefixes?
Maria Chen: Tenant B has a lot of long-form completions and a small set of hot users, but replay showed many cold prefixes (we think env replay scheduling introduced prefix churn). Sequence length median 320, 90th 620. Synthetic test used a flatter seq distribution.
Anita Gomez: Could be two orthogonal issues: 1) kernel selection threshold using avg_seq picks heavier kernels leading to slower matmuls; 2) KV cache thrash because continuous batching delays mix tenants into the same batch and evict entries.
Samir Rao: Confirming on the profiling traces: at seq>384 we fall back to fallback_matmul (less optimized path) ~30% of the time. Also saw increased memcpy overhead when batches contain mixed-length sequences (lots of padding).
perf-bot: flamegraph link: https://go/replay/1833 (contains stack samples, kernel selection events, and KV eviction timeline).
Maria Chen: Repro config (replay harness):
```
mode: replay
tenants: 4
qps_per_tenant: [12, 8, 6, 6]
seq_len_distribution: tenantB: heavy_tail
max_delay_ms: 5
batch_size_cap: 128
batching_heuristic: continuous
kv_cache: enabled
kv_cache_capacity_per_shard: 1e6
```
Jake Patel: For apples-to-apples we should match client inter-arrival distribution between synthetic and replay (current synthetic used Poisson, replay has microbursts). Those microbursts + small max_delay allow big batches to form from mixed tenants -> unfairness.
Tara Liu: Quick experiment ideas:
  1) Increase max_delay_ms -> let tenant B coalesce into its own batch more often (try 10ms, 20ms)
  2) Apply per-tenant batch caps so hot tenants can’t monopolize batch slots (e.g., B cap 32)
  3) Use percentile-based kernel selection (use 95th seq length over window) instead of mean
  4) Tune KV cache eviction to be tenant-aware (pin top-k prefixes for high-churn tenants)
Maria Chen: I'm going to run 3 runs: baseline (current), run A: max_delay_ms=10 + batch_cap=128, run B: max_delay_ms=5 + per_tenant_batch_cap {A:128,B:32,C:64,D:64}, run C: kernel-percentile=95 + kv_pin=enabled. Will push results to the replay dashboard. ETA 3h.
Samir Rao: Add a small synthetic wave that mirrors replay microbursts (burst_size=50, burst_interval=2s) so we can check if the microburst semantics alone cause the regression.
Anita Gomez: Also capture kernel selection logs with this flag when you run: --trace-kernel-decisions=1 and upload perf.data via perf-bot. That helps correlate fallback events to batch composition.
perf-bot: scheduled runs queued: run_1833009123_A, run_1833009123_B, run_1833009123_C. Auto-collect: p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate per tenant, kernel_fallback_count, avg_batch_size, pad_overhead_pct.
Jake Patel: If run B improves fairness but increases overall latency, we should consider adaptive per-tenant caps (controller that shifts caps based on recent tail tradeoffs). Worth prototyping.
Maria Chen: Agreed. I'll start with static caps then we can iterate. Uploading raw traces to https://go/replay/1833/results when done. @Tara please take owner of the percentile kernel experiment if you can.
Tara Liu: On it. Will start in 30m and report back. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: thanks team. TL;DR: tail regression for tenant B likely from mixed-batch KV thrash + kernel fallback at longer seqs. Running three controlled experiments (delay, per-tenant caps, kernel-percentile+kv-pin). Will report numbers and small follow-up doc with suggested heuristics. :eyes:
